# [Baseline] - AND - U - Corporate Device Security

Hardens fully managed and corporate-owned Android devices: six-digit code (numeric complex) that wipes after ten attempts, the code once a day instead of biometrics only, screen on for at most fifteen minutes, Play Protect and automatic app updates on, no file transfer via USB or external storage, no 2G, no manual time, no Private Space and no sharing from work to personal.

| File | [`Baseline_AND_U_Corporate_Device_Security.json`](Baseline_AND_U_Corporate_Device_Security.json) |

> Deliberately `usbdataaccess_disallowusbfiletransfer` and not `disallowusbdatatransfer` (UniFy): the latter blocks all USB data, including wired headsets, docks and Android Auto. Not adopted from the UniFy corporate set: `airplanemodeblocked` (airplane mode impossible), `minimumwifisecuritylevel_personalnetworksecurity` (open and guest networks such as in hotels and trains stop working), `cellularblockwifitethering`, `wifidirectsettings_disallowed`, `ultrawidebandblocked`, `vpnconfigblocked`, `mobilenetworksconfigblocked`, `networkresetblocked` and `cellbroadcastsconfigblocked` (break working from home or travelling, or bring no security gain), `accountsblockmodification` and `certificatecredentialconfigurationdisabled` (first require automatic account provisioning and a SCEP/PKCS profile, UniFy W-5/W-6), `locationmode_enforced` (location always on is a privacy decision), `securitycommoncriteriamodeenabled` (Samsung only, W-25), `passwordexpirationdays` (NIST SP 800-63B), `bluetoothblockcontactsharing` (no more caller name in the car) and `passwordblockkeyguard_true` (that is *Disable lock screen* — an error in UniFy FM). Also not: `appsallowinstallfromunknownsources_false` and `securitydevelopersettingsenabled_false` — for these Android settings `_false` means "not configured", and on device owner devices both are already closed by default. The screen timeout (`screentimeout`, 900 seconds) limits how long the screen stays on; the lock time itself is checked by Compliance Corporate Password. 2G blocking: in regions with only 2G coverage there is no longer any mobile reception; emergency calls keep working. App updates set to `always` also run over mobile data; anyone who wants to test line-of-business apps first chooses `wifionly` or their own update policy (UniFy W-9).
